title: autoscaler: tokenbucket smoothing + utilization reporting + throughput guarantees
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: production fleets have seen repeated capacity thrash during bursty traffic patterns where instantaneous token availability in the token-bucket autoscaler allowed short spikes that triggered scale-ups and subsequent scale-downs. This PR introduces a smoothing layer for the token bucket refill rate (EWMA-based) to reduce impulsive churn, wires utilization EWMA metrics into the utilization reporter, and hooks the autoscaler into throughput-guarantee checks so bursts respect reserved capacity. Changes are backwards-compatible by default and opt-in via config knobs. Implementation notes: 1) Added TokenBucketSmoother that maintains an EWMA of observed refill rates and exposes a smoothedRefill() used by the allocator when deciding token grants. 2) Introduced fleet-level burst_window and max_instant_tokens config options to cap short-lived spikes. 3) Emitted new metrics: autoscaler.tokenbucket_smoothed_rate, autoscaler.fleet_burst_tokens, autoscaler.utilization_ewma_5m, autoscaler.queueing_latency_p95. 4) Integrated throughput guarantees: when a fleet has active throughput guarantees, the smoother will throttle burst grants to ensure guaranteed capacity is not starved. 5) Config schema updated with clear defaults to preserve current behavior unless smoothing is enabled. 6) Tests: unit tests for smoothing math and integration tests simulating burst scenarios. 7) Ops: dashboard/dashboard JSON and docs/ops/dedicated-autoscaler.md updated with recommended tuning values. Backwards-compatibility: default smoothing_alpha=0 (disabled); enabling smoothing is a non-breaking opt-in. Linear items referenced: ENG-4321 (reduce fleet churn from bursts), ENG-4500 (expose utilization ewma). Related: SUP-1234 customer-reported burst impacts.
